name: Populism
summary: Populism, in the leading scholarly definition, is a thin-centred ideology that divides society into a pure people and a corrupt elite and holds that politics should express the people's general will. By itself it offers no programme on economics, culture or foreign affairs, which it takes from host ideologies. Its settled positions are about democracy: popular sovereignty and majority rule, hostility to elites, and rejection of limits on the majority such as separated powers and entrenched minority protections.
scope: The ideational core of populism as the scholarship that defines the name states it: Cas Mudde and Cristobal Rovira Kaltwasser's thin-centred ideology of the pure people against a corrupt elite, with politics as the expression of the people's general will (Mudde 2004, 2017, 2019). Only the core's own claims answer. The economic, cultural and immigration positions of left-wing, right-wing and Latin American variants come from host ideologies (socialism, nationalism, neoliberalism, agrarianism), which are other subjects, so they stay null. The People's Party and its Omaha Platform are not used for answers, since the defining sources mention that party only as an example of popular-sovereignty appeals and do not make its programme a tenet. Excludes the economic-mismanagement, leader-strategy and media-style uses of the term.
